Test taken after 1 September 2025, with scores sent directly by the test organisation
Recommendation letters only from full or associate professors in the intended field
Students and alumni of partner universities apply through their home university

age_requirement: Not specified on the page read
language_requirement: IELTS 7.0 or TOEFL iBT 100, unless exempt

title: Sciences Po Émile Boutmy Scholarship for two-year master's programmes (2027 entry)
overview: Merit-based tuition scholarship for first-time applicants from outside the European Union admitted to a Sciences Po two-year master's programme in Paris. At master's level it is a EUR 18,500 tuition exemption for each of the two years; the 2026-2027 non-EEA master's tuition is EUR 20,640 a year. Applicants request it in the 'Financial information' section of the admission application.
program_dates: Two-year master's programmes starting in autumn 2027
deadline_text: Émile Boutmy page: 'Deadline for master programme: 18 October (1st committee, results before December 20) or 29 November (2nd committee, results before March 2)'; the page gives no year. The international graduate deadlines page lists '29 Nov 2026' as an application-completion date (decision by 11 Feb 2027) and says Boutmy/Mastercard applicants must submit a complete application before the scholarship deadline. The general two-year master's deadline is 21 February 2027, 11:59pm Paris time, but that is too late for the scholarship.
deadline_timezone: Not stated for the scholarship (Paris time is used for programme deadlines)
funding_details: Tuition exemption of EUR 18,500 for each of the two years of the master's
2026-2027 master's tuition for fiscal residents outside the EEA: EUR 20,640 a year, so about EUR 2,140 a year remains payable
Living costs and travel are not mentioned (the page covers tuition only)
participation_fee: Application fee is mandatory ('It is mandatory to pay the application fees'); amount not stated on the pages read; some applicants may be exempted
eligibility: First-time applicant to Sciences Po
National of a non-European Union state whose household does not file taxes within the European Union
Admitted to a two-year master's programme (one-year master's, PhD and exchange candidates are excluded; dual EU citizens, Swiss and Norwegian applicants excluded)
Awarded on merit and the profile sought by the programme, assessed within the admission review
Undergraduate degree of 180 ECTS (bachelor's or equivalent)
nationality_requirements: Non-EU nationals (the DRC qualifies as a non-EU state); no country list
education_requirement: Bachelor's degree or equivalent (180 ECTS); minimum grade averages are set in a spreadsheet that was not read
language_requirement: Language test or exemption required according to the programme's language. French test exemption: at least two consecutive years in the same degree programme taught entirely in French, with proof that French was the only medium of instruction. Native language is not taken into account. A C1 English level must be proven by the end of the master's.
other_requirements: Complete admission file (all documents) by the scholarship deadline; incomplete files are not assessed
documents_required: Online application with 'Financial information' section completed
Transcripts for every year of higher education
CV in French or English depending on the programme
Motivation letter (up to 1,000 words) typed in the form
Academic and professional references through the online form
Language test result or proof of exemption
application_process: Choose a two-year master's programme and check its language and minimum-grade requirements
Apply online and indicate the Émile Boutmy request in the 'Financial information' section
Submit the complete file, fee included, before 29 November

Sciences Po: Deadlines - International graduate admissions (2027 intake)
Sciences Po: Graduate admissions FAQ (documents, minimum degree)

eligibility_reason: As a DRC national with a bachelor's degree the profile meets the non-EU nationality and degree-level criteria. Award depends on admission and merit (grades not recorded), and the French test exemption depends on proof that the Licence was taught entirely in French, which is not recorded.
potential_issues: Covers tuition only: about EUR 2,140 a year of tuition plus all Paris living costs, travel and visa remain at the applicant's expense
Application fee amount not stated
Scholarship page gives deadline dates without a year; the 29 November 2026 date is matched from the deadlines page
Results date differs between pages (before 2 March on the scholarship page, 11 February 2027 on the admissions page)
The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Sciences Po (separate record) offers fuller funding for African applicants
benefits: EUR 37,000 of tuition exemption over two years
Master's at a leading public-policy and international-affairs school
relevance_reason: Strong academic and career fit for policy and public-sector analysis, open to DRC nationals and possibly accessible in French, but it leaves living costs uncovered, so it is useful mainly combined with other funding.
upfront_cost_risk: Application fee, possible language test, then living costs in Paris and the remaining tuition
action: Pick a Sciences Po two-year master's taught in French or bilingually, get a university certificate that the Licence was taught entirely in French, and submit a complete application with the Boutmy request before 29 November 2026; apply in the same cycle to the Mastercard Foundation programme at Sciences Po.

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Sciences Po (two-year master's, 2027 entry)
organization: Sciences Po, with the Mastercard Foundation
overview: Full-need scholarships for African graduates of partner universities to take a two-year master's at Sciences Po in Paris. The only DRC partner institution is the Université de Kinshasa.
deadline_text: Scholarship application deadlines: '23 November 2026 if you wish to receive your master's admission decision by 11 February 2027' and '14 December 2026 if you wish to receive your master's admission decision by 1 April 2027.' No time of day given. Scholars Program results 'will be communicated in April 2027'. (General master's deadline 21 February 2027, 11:59pm Paris time, does not apply: Mastercard applicants 'must submit your application before the deadline of the scholarship'.)
funding_details: 'The Program covers the full financial needs of selected Scholars' (not itemised on the page read)
Application fee waived for eligible candidates
participation_fee: Application fee waived for eligible candidates
eligibility: 'Hold the citizenship of an African country.' Dual citizenship that includes a country outside the African continent is not eligible

'Be currently completing, or already hold, a Bachelor's degree from one of the universities on this list of institutions' (the only DRC institution listed is the Université de Kinshasa); or a Bachelor's plus a recognised bridge or mentoring programme of an approved organisation; or a Bachelor's plus current or past UNHCR refugee status
'Be under 35 years of age on 1 September of the year in which the scholarship application is submitted.'
'Not already hold, or currently pursuing, a Master's degree'; applying to the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program for the first time
Students currently enrolled in, or graduated from, a French higher education institution are not eligible
age_requirement: Under 35 on 1 September of the year in which the scholarship application is submitted (an application made in 2026 is measured on 1 September 2026)
education_requirement: Bachelor's (completed or in progress) from a partner institution (DRC: Université de Kinshasa only), or a Bachelor's plus a recognised bridge or mentoring programme, or a Bachelor's plus UNHCR refugee status
other_requirements: Create the Master's application on the Sciences Po admissions platform at the same time as the eligibility request; otherwise the application-fee waiver is lost 'even if you are found eligible for the scholarship at a later stage'
application_process: Submit the two-year Sciences Po master's application with the Mastercard Foundation scholarship application by 23 November 2026 (decision by 11 February 2027) or 14 December 2026 (decision by 1 April 2027)
eligibility_reason: Citizenship, age and degree level fit, but eligibility depends on the bachelor's coming from a partner institution. The DRC's only one is the Université de Kinshasa, and the profile does not record the awarding university.
potential_issues: Restricted to graduates of listed partner universities (the only DRC institution listed is the Université de Kinshasa), or Bachelor's holders with a recognised bridge or mentoring programme or UNHCR refugee status
Two scholarship deadlines (23 November and 14 December 2026); no time of day is stated

The general international admissions deadlines page lists 29 November 2026 for a decision before 11 February 2027; scholarship applicants must meet the earlier date on the scholarship page (23 November 2026)
The Master's application must be created at the same time as the eligibility request, or the application-fee waiver is lost
Funding is described as covering 'the full financial needs of selected Scholars' without an itemised list
Deferring admission makes the applicant ineligible
Dual citizenship that includes a non-African country, and current or former students of French higher-education institutions, are not eligible
benefits: Two-year Sciences Po master's in Paris
relevance_reason: Public policy at Sciences Po, in French or English, is a strong thematic fit; access depends entirely on the awarding university.
action: If your Licence is from the Université de Kinshasa, create your two-year master's application on the Sciences Po platform and send the Scholars Program eligibility request at the same time, then apply by 23 November 2026 (14 December 2026 at the latest). Otherwise skip.
notes: Previously on the research watchlist. 19 October 2026 (source_changed flag): the page now publishes two scholarship deadlines (23 November and 14 December 2026) and an April 2027 results date; the earlier 'October to mid-December 2026' fee-waiver wording is no longer on the page. 29 October 2026: the scholarship page was re-read in full; the age rule is measured on 1 September of the year in which the scholarship application is submitted (the earlier record read 1 September 2027, a year the page does not give).

title: World Food Forum Youth Policy Board 2027-2028
overview: Independent board of 40 young changemakers aged 18-35 that leads the WFF Youth Assembly's policy work: regional and thematic youth consultations, policy recommendations, and youth representation in FAO and intergovernmental processes, including preparation for the 2028 FAO Regional Conferences. One-year term, about 25 hours a month, mostly remote.
program_dates: One-year term, 2027-2028 cohort (option to reapply for a second year); at least one weekly 1-hour meeting between 09:00 and 18:00 CEST/CET.
deadline_text: Reported by secondary sources: deadline November 30, 2026 (Opportunity Desk). The official call page embeds a Microsoft Form that could not be read, and the official Terms of Reference give no deadline.
funding_details: The official Terms of Reference describe duties and a 25-hours-a-month commitment but mention no payment, stipend or travel support
Members may 'represent the YPB in relevant intergovernmental processes and conferences'; who pays for any travel is not stated
eligibility: Have graduated from high school and either have completed or be enrolled in a bachelor's degree programme at the time of application
Be between 18 and 35 years as of 30 April 2027
Be national of an FAO Member State
Proficiency in spoken and written English at C1 level (fluency in other FAO official languages is an advantage)
Available for at least one weekly 1-hour YPB meeting between 09:00-18:00 CEST/CET
Demonstrated experience, knowledge or strong engagement in agrifood systems, policy advocacy and youth empowerment
About 25 hours per month (20 core area, 5 supporting area)
Ability to work in an international, multicultural environment
Not immediate family of FAO employees; not employed by FAO; not a current or former WFF YSG or YPB member
nationality_requirements: National of an FAO Member State (the Democratic Republic of the Congo has been an FAO Member since 9 November 1961, per FAO's membership page)
education_requirement: High school graduate and a completed or ongoing bachelor's degree
experience_requirement: Demonstrated experience, knowledge or strong engagement in agrifood systems, policy advocacy and youth empowerment
language_requirement: English at C1 level (spoken and written); other FAO languages an advantage
other_requirements: Preference for experience in youth constituencies or organisations, consultative youth processes, underrepresented stakeholder backgrounds (farmers, Indigenous Peoples, women) and understanding of international agrifood governance
documents_required: Round 2 (shortlisted): CV, a letter of recommendation and a two-minute video
application_process: Fill in the online form on the WFF Youth Policy Board call page
Round 1: Secretariat scores eligibility and experience
Round 2: committee shortlist; CV, recommendation letter and two-minute video requested

WFF Youth Policy Board open call (embedded form)

eligibility_reason: Nationality (DRC is an FAO Member), the bachelor's degree and the age limit are met. The profile records no evidence of C1 English and no experience in agrifood systems, policy advocacy or youth empowerment, both of which are stated criteria.
potential_issues: Deadline (30 November 2026) comes only from an aggregator; the official form could not be read
No payment or travel support mentioned: treat it as an unpaid volunteer role
C1 English must be demonstrated; how is not stated
The ToR heading for thematic duties says '2026-2027 term' inside the 2027-2028 document (likely a copy error)
benefits: Policy role inside an FAO platform
Representation of youth in FAO and intergovernmental processes

notes: Official page says the board is selected by peers and the 2026 cohort is the fifth. The ToR (2027-2028) was read in full; it has no deadline, no funding section and no time zone for the deadline.

Between the ages of 24 and 45 during the programme
